translations.text: King David grew old and reached the end of his days. They covered him with clothes, but he could not get warm.
His servants said to him: "Let them bring a young virgin to our lord the king. Let her stand before the king and serve him, and let her care for him, so that the king may always be kept warm."
They searched all through Israel for a very beautiful young girl. They found Abishag the Shunammite and brought her to the king.
The girl was very beautiful. She lay beside the king and served him, but the king did not know her.
Adonijah, David's son, set himself up as king in David's place. He got himself chariots and horsemen, and fifty men to run ahead of him.
His father never rebuked him at all by saying, "Why are you like this?" or "Why are you doing this?" He was very handsome, and he had been born after Absalom.
He made his plans with Joab, and Abiathar supported him.
But Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, and Shimei with his companions, who were David's chosen men, did not side with Adonijah.

Adonijah held a great [?]. He slaughtered cattle and sheep by the stone of Zoheleth, which is near En-rogel. He invited all his brothers, the king's sons, and all the king's men of Judah, David's servants.
But he did not invite Nathan, Benaiah (the king's counsellors) or Solomon.
Nathan came to Bathsheba, Solomon's mother, and said to her: "Have you not heard that Adonijah son of Haggith has become king, and our lord David does not know?
Now come, let me give you some advice, so that you may save your own life and the life of your son Solomon.

Go in now to King David and say to him: 'My lord the king, did you not swear to your handmaid by the Lord God, saying: "Your son Solomon shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne"? Why then has Adonijah become king?'
While you are still speaking with the king, I will come in after you and confirm your words."
Bathsheba went in to the king's bedchamber. The king was old and far advanced in days, and he was sitting, and Abishag the Shunammite was standing before the king to serve him.
Bathsheba came in and bowed down low before the king. The king said to her: "What do you want?"
Bathsheba answered him: "My lord the king, you swore by the Lord God and said: 'Your son Solomon shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne.'
Now Adonijah has become king, and you, my lord the king, do not know it.
He has slaughtered a great number of cattle and sheep. He has invited all the king's sons, Abiathar the priest and Joab the commander of the army. He has done this without my lord the king.
Now if this matter comes from you, and it pleases you, my lord the king, let it be made known before all this people who will sit on the throne of my lord the king after him.
Otherwise, when my lord the king rests with his fathers, Solomon and I will be counted as offenders."
While she was still speaking, Nathan the prophet arrived at that very moment. He had just reached the doors.
They told the king: "Nathan the prophet is standing at the doors." When Nathan came in before the king, he bowed down with his face to the ground.
And he said: Did you, the king, command and say, "After me Solomon shall reign, and he shall sit on my throne"?

For today he has gone down and has sacrificed oxen and sheep and a great many lambs, and Adonijah has invited all the king's sons, and Joab, your commander-in-chief, and Abiathar the high priest, and the commanders of your army. And they are making merry and rejoicing before him and saying: "Long live King Adonijah!"
But I, your servant, and Zadok the high priest, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and Solomon your son, have not been invited.
And if this word came from you, from our lord the king, why did you not make known to us, your servants, who would sit on the throne of our lord after you?
David answered and said: Call Bathsheba in here! And Bathsheba came in before the king.
The king began to swear an oath and said: As my Lord lives, who has delivered me from all my afflictions,
as I swore to you before by the Lord God of Israel, saying, "Solomon my son shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne in my place," so I will do this very day.
And Bathsheba bowed down with her face to the ground before the king and said: May King David live forever!
And the king summoned Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet and Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and they came in before the king.
And King David said to them: Take with you the servants of your lord, and set Solomon my son on my own mule, and bring him down to Gihon.
And let Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anoint him there over all Israel and Judah, and blow the trumpet before him and say: "May King Solomon live forever!"
And let him come up here again, and you with him; and let him come in and sit on my throne, and let him reign in my place. And I will give him the command to reign over all Judah and Israel.
Benaiah son of Jehoiada began to speak to the king and said: So be it, and may the Lord confirm the word of my lord the king. As the Lord your God has spoken to you, so may my lord the king do.
And as the Lord God was with my lord the king, so may he be with Solomon, and may he establish his throne as he established the throne of my lord David.
And Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet and Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and the Cherethites and the Pelethites went down, and they set Solomon on King David's mule and brought him down to Gihon.
And Zadok the high priest took the horn of oil from the tent and anointed Solomon. And they blew the trumpet, and all the people said: May King Solomon live forever!
And all the people followed him, and the king's servants danced and [?] before him and rejoiced with great joy, and the earth resounded with the noise of their shouting.

And Adonijah and all who were with him at his feast, eating and drinking, heard it, and their merriment broke off [?]. And when Joab heard the sound of the uproar, he said: What is this sound of great uproar?

And while he was still saying this, at that very moment Jonathan son of Abiathar the high priest arrived, and Adonijah said to him: Come in, for you are a worthy man, and you must be bringing good news.
Jonathan answered Adonijah and said to him: "Our lord King David has made Solomon king.
He sent with him Zadok the high priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and the Cherethites and the Pelethites, and they set him on the king's mule.
Zadok the high priest and Nathan the prophet anointed him king and brought him up with royal rejoicing, and the whole land resounded with their noise. That is the noise you were hearing.
And Solomon sat on the king's throne.

All the people went and blessed our lord David. They went in before him alone and said to him: 'May the Lord make the name of your son Solomon more glorious than your name, and exalt his throne above your throne.' When the king heard this, he bowed down in worship on his bed.
And he said: 'Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, who has given me the offspring of my own body to sit on my throne, and has let me see it with my own eyes.'"
When they heard this, all who had been feasting with Adonijah were alarmed. They got up and each went his own way.

Adonijah was afraid of Solomon. He rushed into the court of the Lord, clung to the altar of the Lord, and said: "Let King Solomon swear to me today that he will not put me, his servant, to death with the sword."

They told Solomon, saying: "Adonijah is afraid of King Solomon and has clung to the altar of God, and he says: 'Let King Solomon swear to me today that he will not put his servant to death with the sword.'"
Solomon answered and said: "If he proves strong in wisdom and righteousness, not one hair of his will fall to the ground. But if any evil deed is found in him, he will die."
Solomon sent, and they brought him down from the altar.
Solomon sat on the throne of his father David at twelve years of age, and his kingdom prospered.
Adonijah son of Haggith went in to Bathsheba, Solomon's mother, and bowed down to her. She said to him: "Do you come in peace?" He said: "In peace."
He said to her: "I have something to say to you." Bathsheba said to him: "Speak."
He said: "You yourself know that the kingdom was mine, and all Israel had set their faces on me to be king. But the kingdom turned away and became my brother's, for it was his from the Lord.
Now I ask one small request of you; do not turn your face away from me." Bathsheba said to him: "Speak."
Adonijah said to her: "Speak to your son King Solomon, for he will not turn his face away from you, and let him give me Abishag the Shunammite as wife."
Bathsheba said to him: "Very well; I will speak to the king on your behalf."

Bathsheba went in to King Solomon to speak on behalf of Adonijah. King Solomon rose up to meet her, kissed her, and sat down again on his throne. They set a seat for the king's mother, and she sat at his right hand.
She said to him: "I ask one small request of you; do not turn your face away from me." The king said to her: "Ask, my mother, for I will not turn my face away from you."
She said: "Let Abishag the Shunammite be given to your brother Adonijah as wife."

King Solomon answered his mother: "Why are you asking for Abishag the Shunammite to be given to Adonijah as his wife? Ask for the kingdom for him as well, since he is my elder brother, and Abiathar the priest is on his side, and so is Joab son of Zeruiah, the commander, who is his friend."
And King Solomon swore by God and said: "May God do this to me and add more to it, for Adonijah has spoken this word to his own harm."
"And now, as the Lord lives, who has established me and set me on the throne of David my father, and has made my name as the Lord told me, Adonijah shall surely die today."
And King Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and he killed Adonijah. And Adonijah died on that day.

And King Solomon said to Abiathar the priest: "Go to Anathoth, to your estate, to your house. You deserve to die today, but I will not put you to death, because you carried the ark of the covenant of God before my father, and because you suffered in everything in which my father was afflicted."
And King Solomon drove him out, so that he would no longer be priest of the Lord, in fulfilment of the word of the Lord that he had spoken about the house of Eli in Shiloh.
And Joab son of Zeruiah heard of this, for Joab had sided with Adonijah and not with Solomon. And Joab fled into the tent of the Lord and took hold of the horns of the altar.

And they told Solomon: "Joab has fled into the tent of the Lord and has taken hold of the horns of the altar." And Solomon sent to Joab and said: "What has happened to you, that you have fled to the altar?" And Joab said: "Because I was afraid of you, and I fled to the Lord." And King Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada and said to him: "Go, kill him and bury him."

And Benaiah son of Jehoiada went into the tent of the Lord and said to him: "The king says: 'Come out.'" And Joab said: "I will not go out from here; I will die here." And Benaiah son of Jehoiada went back and told the king: "This is what Joab said, and this is how he answered me."
The king said to him: "Go and do to him as he said: kill him and bury him. And you shall wipe away from me and from my father's house the blood that he shed without cause."

"God has brought that unjustly shed blood back on his own head, because he attacked two men who were righteous and better than he was and killed them with the sword, and my father did not know of it: the blood of Abner son of Ner, commander of Israel, and of Amasa son of Jether, commander of Judah."
"And their blood shall come back on his head and on the head of his descendants forever. But may there be peace from the Lord forever for David and his descendants, his house and his throne."
And Benaiah son of Jehoiada rose up, attacked him and killed him, and buried him in the tomb in the wilderness.

And King Solomon appointed Benaiah son of Jehoiada over the people in place of Joab, and his kingdom prospered in Jerusalem. And King Solomon appointed Zadok the priest as priest and chief in place of Abiathar. On the wisdom and knowledge of Solomon
And the Lord gave Solomon knowledge and very great wisdom, and a breadth of heart like the sand on the seashore.
And Solomon's understanding grew greater than the wisdom of all those born before him, and greater than the wisdom of the Egyptians.

On the taking of a wife. And Solomon took Pharaoh's daughter as his wife, and brought her into the city of David until he had finished building his own house, and first the house of the Lord, and the wall of Jerusalem all around. He built and finished them in seven years.
And Solomon had sixty thousand burden-bearers and eighty thousand stonecutters in the mountains.

And Solomon made the sea, the stands, the great basins, the very great pillars and the water channels of the court. And he finished the height [?] by fortifying it [?], and he cut through the city of David.
And then Pharaoh's daughter went out from the city of David to her own house, which he had built for her, and only then did he finish it [?] himself.
And three times a year Solomon offered whole [?] sacrifices on the altar that he had built to the Lord, and burned incense before the Lord. And he finished the temple.
And these are the chief officers in charge of King Solomon's work: three thousand seven hundred taskmasters over the people who did the work.
And he built Asud, Megiddo, Gezer, Beth-horon, Ano and Beldad.
He built these cities round about after the house of the Lord and the wall of Jerusalem.
And while he was still alive, David gave Solomon a command and said to him: "Look, you have with you Shimei, son of Gera, son of Jemini, from Gabath.
He cursed me with a painful curse on the day I was going out to the camps.
And he came out to meet me at the Jordan, and I swore to him by the Lord and said: 'I will not kill you with the sword.'
Now do not let him go unpunished, for you are a wise man. Consider what you will do to him, and send his old age down to hell with blood."
And the king sent and summoned Shimei, son of Gera, and said to him: "Make yourself a house in Jerusalem and live there, and do not go out anywhere.
And on the day you go out, if you cross the brook Kidron, know for certain that you will die, and your blood will be on your own head." And the king made him swear on that day.
And Shimei said to the king: "What you have said is good, my lord the king; your servant will do so." And Shimei lived in Jerusalem for three years.
And after three years two of Shimei's servants ran away and went to Achish, son of Maacah, king of the Gittites. And people told Shimei: "Look, those two servants of yours are in Gath."
And Shimei arose and set [?] on his [?], and went to Achish in Gath to ask for his servants. And Shimei went and brought his servants back from Gath.
And people told Solomon: "Shimei went to Gath and brought back his servants."

And the king sent and summoned Shimei and said to him: "Did I not make you swear by the Lord, and lay a charge on you, and say: 'On the day you go out from Jerusalem and go to the right or to the left, know for certain that you shall surely die'? And you said to me: 'What I have heard is good.'
Now why have you not kept the oath of the Lord and the command that I gave you?"
And the king said to Shimei: "You yourself know all your wickedness, which your heart knows, all that you did to my father David. And the Lord has brought that evil back on your own head."
And King Solomon is blessed, and the throne of David shall stand before the Lord forever.
And King Solomon gave orders to Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and he went out and killed him. And Shimei died.

When Solomon's kingship had been made secure, Solomon made a marriage alliance with Pharaoh, king of the Egyptians. He asked for his daughter and brought her into the City of David, until he had finished building his own house, the temple of the Lord, and the wall around Jerusalem.
And the people burned incense at the high places, because the temple for the name of the Lord had not yet been built up to that day.
And Solomon loved the Lord, walking in the commandments of his father David; but he too offered sacrifices and burned incense at the high places.

And the king rose and went to Gibeon to sacrifice there, because it was the highest and greatest high place. He offered a thousand sacrifices on the altar at Gibeon. Concerning the vision of the Lord in sleep.
And the Lord appeared to Solomon in his sleep at night, and the Lord said to Solomon: "Ask whatever you would ask for yourself."

And Solomon said: "You showed great mercy to your servant David, my father, because he walked before you in truth and righteousness and uprightness of heart toward you. And you kept this great mercy for him, to give him a son to sit on his thrones, as it is this very day.
And now, O my Lord, you have given me, your servant, in place of David my father; and I am a little child and do not know how to go out or come in.
And your servant is in the midst of your people whom you have chosen, as countless in number as the sand of the sea.
Give your servant an understanding heart to hear and to judge your people in righteousness, to discern between good and evil; for who is able to judge this great people of yours?"
And the word was pleasing to the Lord, that Solomon had asked for this thing.

And the Lord said to him: "Because you have asked this thing of me, and have not asked for yourself long life, nor riches, nor the lives of your enemies, but have asked for yourself wisdom to discern righteous judgment,

behold, I have done according to your word, and I will give you a heart of wisdom and knowledge, so that there has been no one like you among those before you, and after you there shall be no one like you.
And what you did not ask for I will also give [?] you, riches and glory, so that there has been no one like you among the kings.
And if you walk in my ways, keeping my commandments, as David your father walked, I will lengthen your days."

And Solomon awoke, and behold, it was a vision. And he rose and went into Jerusalem and stood before the altar, in front of the ark in Zion. And he offered burnt offerings [?] and peace offerings, and made a great feast for himself and for all his servants.
At that time two women who were harlots came before King Solomon and stood before him.
And one of the women said: "Hear me, my lord! This woman and I were living in one house, and I gave birth in that house.
And it happened that three days after I gave birth, this woman also gave birth. And we were alone in the house, and no one else was in the house with us.
And this woman's child died, because she lay on it.
And she got up in the middle of the night and stole my child from my arms while your handmaid was asleep. She laid him in her own bosom, and her own dead child she laid in my bosom.
And I got up to nurse my child, and he was dead. And at dawn I looked, and it was not the child I had borne.

And the other woman said: "No, your son is the dead one, and my son is the living one." And the first one said: "No, the dead one is yours, and the living one is mine." And this is what they said before the king.
And the king said: "You say, 'My son is the living one, and her son is the dead one.' And she says, 'No, your son is the dead one, and my son is this living one.'"
And the king said: "Bring me a sword!" And they brought a sword before the king.
And the king said: "Cut this living nursing child in two, and give half of him to one and half of him to the other."

And the woman whose child was the living one answered and spoke to the king, for her womb was moved with pity for her son, and she said: "I beg you, O king! Give her this living child, and do not put him to death." But the other said: "Let him be neither mine nor hers; cut him in two."
The king answered and said: "Give the living child to this woman, the one who said, 'Give him to her and do not put him to death,' for she is his mother."
All Israel heard of this judgment that the king had given, and the people were afraid before the face of the king, for they saw that the wisdom of God was with him to do justice.
And King Solomon was king over Israel.
And these are his chief officials: Azariah son of Zadok, the priest;
Eliab and Ahijah, sons of Shaphat, scribes; and Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud;
and Benaiah son of Jehoiada, commander of the army; Zadok and Abiathar, priests;
and Ornia son of Nathan, over the officers; and Zakor son of Nathan, priest, the king's friend;
and Ahiel the steward; and Eliab son of Jehoiada, over the people; and Adoniram son of Edram, over the tribute.
And Solomon had twelve officers appointed over Israel, to manage and lead and to supply provisions for the royal household; each of them had to supply provisions for one month in the year.
And these are their names: Beor son of Hur, in the hill country of Ephraim;
the son of Rechab, in Makmas and Salamin and Beth-shemesh and Edom, as far as Beth-nad;
Machir son of Ekoreb, in Bethnam and Lozah and Amika and Pharakin;
and Andab and Mantam and Phatis [?], one man, whose [wife was?] Tabaath, daughter of Solo[mon] [?]
[?] ... and of the stands, and the height of their wheels was a cubit and a half.
And the workmanship of their wheels was like the workmanship of chariot wheels; and their hands, their necks, their shoulders and all their workmanship were of cast bronze.
There were four shoulder-pieces on the four corners of the stand, and its shoulder-pieces were made of one piece with the stand itself.
And on the top of the stand there was a half cubit in height, round all about, on the top of the stand; and its hands projected from the stand itself.
And on the setting of its hands and on its panels [?] were engraved cherubim and lions and palm trees, fashioned from it, facing one another, inside and outside.
And in its likeness he made all the workmanship of the ten stands: one measure, one proportion and one form belonged to all of them.
And he made ten pot-shaped basins of bronze, and one basin held forty mar [?]. And the measure of the basins was four cubits, and there was one basin on each of the ten stands.
And he set the stands, five on the right side of the house and five on the left side of the house. And he set the sea on the right side, toward the sunrise, and [?].
And Hiram made the pots, the cauldrons for heating, and the bowls. And Hiram finished all the work that he did for King Solomon in the house of the Lord.
And two pillars, with carved work set all around on the two capitals of the pillars, and two networks each to cover the carved work all around, upon the capitals that had been made.

And four hundred pomegranate-shaped ornaments for the two networks, and pomegranate-shaped ornaments set in two rows on each network, to cover all around the two works [?] of the stand, upon the same two pillars.
And the ten pot-shaped basins on the stands.
The one sea, and the twelve oxen under the sea.

And the three heating pots, the bowls and the vessels that Hiram made for King Solomon for the house of the Lord: forty-eight pillars for the house of the Lord and for the house of the king. And all the work that Hiram did was of bronze only.
And there was no equal to the bronze from which he made all that work, many very great things, and there was no equal to the brilliance of that bronze.
And it was at the bank of the Jordan that he did the bronze casting for the king, in the thick earth, between Succoth and Zarethan.

And King Solomon gave all of it, for it was exceedingly great in quantity, and there was no counting the bronze. And Solomon made all the vessels of service for the house of the Lord: the altars of gold, and the table on which the bread of offering was set out was of gold.
And the lampstands, five on the right and five on the left, in front of the inner sanctuary, of choice gold; and the lamps, the lights and the tongs of gold.

And the frames [?], the snuffers [?], the basins, the dishes and the censers [?] of choice gold; and the hinges [?] of the inner house, the Holy of Holies, and the doors of the temple, overlaid with choice gold.

And all the work that King Solomon did for the house of the Lord was completed. And Solomon brought in the holy things of David his father and all the holy things of Solomon, the silver and the gold, and he gave all the vessels as treasure to the house of the Lord.

At that time King Solomon gathered all the elders of Israel together with all the chiefs, according to the order of the fathers of the sons of Israel, to bring the ark of the Lord up to Zion from the city of David.
And all the sons of Israel assembled before King Solomon in the month of Ethanim, which is the seventh month.
And all the elders of Israel came out, and the priests took up the ark of the Lord.
And the priests and the Levites took up the tent of witness and all the holy vessels of service that were in the tent of witness.
King Solomon and all the people of the children of Israel were gathered together with him before the ark, and they were sacrificing oxen and sheep, countless in number.
And the priests brought the ark of the covenant into its place, into the inner sanctuary (dabir), the house of the Holy of Holies, under the wings of the cherubim.
The wings were spread out over the place where the ark stood, and the cherubim covered the ark and its holy things from above.
And they stood over the holy things, and the ends of the consecrated ones were seen from the holy place, facing the inner sanctuary (dabir), but they were not visible outside.

And there was nothing in the ark except the two tablets of stone, the tablets of the covenant, which Moses had placed in it at Horeb, the covenant which the Lord made after they came out of the land of the Egyptians.
And it came to pass, when the priests came out of the holy place, that the temple of God was filled with a cloud.
And the priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud, for the temple was filled with the glory of the Lord.
At that time Solomon began to speak and said: The Lord said that he would be a shelter in the mist.
And I have built him a temple as a dwelling place, and for the establishing of his throne forever.
And the king turned around and blessed all the people of Israel who were standing there.
And Solomon said: Blessed is the Lord God of Israel today, who spoke with his own mouth concerning David my father, and has fulfilled it with his own hand. And he said:

From the day that I brought my people Israel out of the land of Egypt, I did not choose any one of the cities, the portion of Israel, to build my house, but I chose David to be leader of my people Israel.
And it was in the heart of David my father to build a temple for the name of the Lord God of Israel.
And the Lord said to David my father: Because it came into his heart to build a temple for my name, it is good that it came into your heart.
But you shall not build the temple; rather your son, who will come forth from your loins [?], he shall build the house for my name.

And the Lord has fulfilled the word that he spoke, and the Lord has raised me up in place of David my father, and has set me on the throne of Israel, as the Lord said, and I have built the house for the name of the Lord God of Israel.
And I have prepared there a place for the ark of the law of the Lord to stand, the covenant which the Lord made with our fathers when he brought them out of the land of the Egyptians.
And Solomon stood facing the altar of the Lord, before all the people of Israel, and lifted up his hands to heaven.
And he said: O Lord, God of Israel, there is no God like you in heaven above or on earth below, you who have kept the covenant with your servant who walked before you with all his heart.
You have kept it with your servant David my father, as you spoke to him and said with your mouth, and you have fulfilled it with your hand, as it is this very day.

And now, O Lord, God of Israel, keep for your servant David my father what you spoke to him and said: There shall not fail you a man before my face to sit on the throne of Israel, if only your children take heed to their ways, to walk before me as you have walked before me.
And now, O Lord, God of Israel, let your word be made sure, the word which you spoke to your servant David, my father.
And will God truly dwell among men upon the earth? If the heavens and the heaven of heavens cannot contain you, how then can this house which I have built for your name be a dwelling place for you?
And now look upon the prayer of your servant and upon my supplication, O Lord, God of Israel, and hear the prayer of your servant, who stands before you, with you, today.
Let your eyes be open to look day and night upon this place, of which you said: "Let my name be there to hear the prayer" with which your servant entreats you in that place day and night.
And may you hear the voice of my prayer and of your people Israel, who will worship you in this place. Hear in the place of your dwelling in heaven, and grant forgiveness.
If any man sins against his neighbour, and someone lays a curse on another and he confesses before the altar of this temple,

then may you hear from heaven and act, and judge your people Israel: condemn the lawlessness of the lawless, repaying upon his head the recompense of his ways, and justify the righteous, repaying him according to his own righteousness.

When your people Israel are struck down before their enemies because they have sinned against you, and they turn back to you and confess your name and pray and make supplication to you in that temple,
then may you hear from heaven and forgive the sins of your people Israel, and bring them back to their land, which you gave to their fathers.
When the rain is held back and there is no rain, because they have sinned against you, and they pray in this place and confess your name and turn from their sins when you have brought them low,

then may you hear from heaven and forgive the sins of your people Israel, and show them the good ways in which they should walk, and give rain upon your land, which you gave to your people as an inheritance.

And if there is famine in the land, or death, or burning by fire, or caterpillar [?], or locust, or blight [?], or if an enemy oppresses them in one of their cities, and whatever calamity and whatever affliction there may be,
and whatever request and petition in prayer is made by any man or by all your people Israel, when each one knows the pain of his own heart and stretches out his hands toward this temple,
then may you hear from heaven, from your prepared dwelling place, and forgive, and deal with each according to his ways, since you know his heart, for you alone know the hearts of all men,
so that they may fear you all the days that they live upon the face of the land which you gave to our fathers.
And the foreigner, who is not of your people Israel but has come from a distant land,
where he has heard of your great name and of your mighty hand and your outstretched arm, and he comes and worships in this place,

then may you hear from heaven, from your prepared dwelling place, and do according to everything for which that foreigner prays to you, so that all the nations of the earth may know your name and fear you, as your people Israel do, and may know that your name is called upon this temple which I have built.

And if your people go out to battle against their enemies on the way by which I send them, and they pray to the name of the Lord toward the way of the city that you have chosen and the temple that I have built for your name,
hear their prayer and their supplication from heaven, and give them justice and peace,

when they sin against you, for there is no one who does not sin against you. And if you send [it] upon them and hand them over to their enemies, and their captors carry them away captive to the land of the enemies, whether far or near,

and they turn back their [literally: your] hearts in the land to which they were carried captive, and they repent and plead with you in the land of their captivity and say, 'We have sinned, we have acted lawlessly, we have done wrong,'

and they turn back with all their heart and all their strength in the land of the enemies to which they were carried captive, and they pray to you that they may return to their own land, which you gave to their fathers, and for the city that I built for your name,
then hear their prayer and their supplication from heaven, from your prepared dwelling place, and give them justice.
Forgive the wicked deeds by which they sinned against you, and all the insults with which they insulted you. Let them find mercy in the sight of all who carried them captive, and show them mercy,
for they are your people and your inheritance, whom you brought out of the land of the Egyptians, out of the middle of the iron-smelting furnace.
Let your eyes and your ears be attentive to the prayer of your servant and to the prayer of your people Israel, to hear them in all that we ask of you,
for you chose them out of all the peoples of the earth to be your inheritance, as you said to your servant Moses when you brought our fathers out of Egypt, O Lord, Lord!

Then Solomon began to speak, and he said this about the temple when he had finished it: 'The Lord set the sun in the heavens, and he said he would dwell in thick cloud. Build me a beautiful house to dwell in anew.' Look, is not all this written in the books of the singers of praise?
When Solomon had finished offering all this prayer to the Lord, he rose from before the altar of the Lord, where he had been kneeling on his knees with his hands spread out toward heaven.
He stood up and turned to the people and blessed all Israel in a loud voice, saying:
"Blessed be the Lord God today, who has given rest to his people Israel, just as he promised. Not one word of all the good words he spoke to his servant Moses has failed.
May the Lord be with us as he was with our fathers, and may he not abandon us
to hearts that turn away from walking in all his ways and from keeping all his commandments and his judgments, which he commanded our fathers.

And may these words of mine, which I have prayed before the Lord my God, be presented before him day and night, so that he may give justice to me, this servant of yours, and give justice to your people Israel day by day,
so that all the peoples of the earth may know that you are the Lord God and there is no other besides you."
Let our minds be perfect toward the Lord our God, so that we walk in purity according to his commands and keep his judgments, as on this day.
And the king and all Israel with him were offering sacrifices before the Lord.

And King Solomon offered the sacrifice of peace offerings that he offered to the Lord: twenty-two thousand oxen and one hundred and twenty thousand sheep. And the king and all the sons of Israel performed the dedication of the house of the Lord

on that day. And the king consecrated the court that was in front of the temple of the Lord, for there he made the whole burnt offerings, the offerings and the fat of the peace offerings, because the altar that stood before the Lord was too small and could not hold the whole burnt offerings of the peace offerings.

And on that day Solomon held a feast, and all Israel with him, a great assembly from the entrance of Hamath to the river of Egypt, before the Lord our God. They ate and drank and rejoiced in the temple that he had built before the Lord God, seven days and seven nights: fourteen days.

And on the eighth day he dismissed the people. They blessed the king and went each to his own inheritance with gladness of heart, rejoicing over all the good things that the Lord had done for David his servant and for his people Israel.
And it came to pass, when Solomon had finished building the temple of the Lord and the king's house and all the work that Solomon had wished to do,
that the Lord appeared to Solomon a second time, as he had appeared to him at Gibeon.

And the Lord said to him: "I have heard your voice and your prayers and your petitions that you made before me. I have done for you according to your prayer: I have consecrated this temple that you built, to set my name on it forever. And my eyes and my heart shall be there all the days.
And as for you, if you walk before me as David your father walked, in purity of heart and uprightness, to do everything that I commanded them, and if you keep my ordinances and my commandments,
I will establish the throne of your kingdom over Jerusalem forever, as I spoke to David your father, saying: 'You shall not lack a man to lead Israel.'
But if you and your children turn back from me and do not keep my commandments and my ordinances which Moses [?] gave you before you, and you go and serve foreign gods and bow down to them,
I will remove Israel from the land that I gave them, and this house that I consecrated for my name I will cast out of my sight. And Israel shall be a ruin and a byword among all peoples.
And this temple, made so lofty: all who pass by it will be astonished and will hiss, and they will say: 'Why has the Lord done this to this land and to this temple?'

And they will say: 'Because they forsook the Lord their God, who brought their fathers out of Egypt, out of the house of bondage, and they followed foreign gods, bowed down to them and served them. Therefore he has brought all this evil upon them.'" At that time Solomon brought Pharaoh's daughter up from the city of David to his house, which he had built for himself.
And it happened in those days, in the twentieth year, that Solomon built the two houses: the house of the Lord and the house of the king.
And Hiram, king of Tyre, helped Solomon with pine and fir timber, with gold, and with everything he wished. At that time King Solomon gave Hiram twenty cities in Galilee.
And Hiram went out from Tyre to Galilee to see the cities that Solomon had given him, and they did not please him.
He said to him: "What are these cities that you have given me, brother?" And he called them "Border" to this day.
And Hiram brought Solomon a hundred and two weights of gold.

And this is the tribute that the king levied to build the house of the Lord, the house of the king, the Millo and the high places. And he rebuilt the ruined walls of the city of David, and the [?], and the open square, and the wall of Jerusalem, and Hazor, Megiddo and Gezer

of the king of the Egyptians: for he had come up and plundered Gezer and burned it with fire, and he slaughtered the Canaanites who lived in that city, and he gave it as a dowry to his daughter, Solomon's wife.
And Solomon built Gezer and Lower Beth-horon,
and Baalath, and Thermoth in the wilderness; those too [?] he built,
all the cities for settlement that belonged to Solomon, the cities for chariots, and all the cities for horsemen. And all the work that he did in Jerusalem, in Lebanon and in all the land, he [?]
on all the remaining people of the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Canaanites, the Hivites, the Jebusites and the Girgashites, who were not of the sons of Israel.
And their sons who were left in the land, whom the sons of Israel had not been able to destroy, Solomon put to forced labour as tribute, to this day.
But Solomon did not put the sons of Israel under heavy tribute, for they were men of war and his servants, and their sons were commanders, armed men and horsemen.
And these were the chiefs whom Solomon had set over the work: five hundred and fifty over the people who did the work.
But Pharaoh's daughter went up from the city of David to her own house, which he had built for her; at that time he built the Millo.

And three times a year Solomon offered whole burnt offerings and peace offerings on the altar that he had built to the Lord, and he burned incense before the Lord. And he finished the work of the house.
And King Solomon built a ship at Ezion-geber, which is near Elath, on the shore of the farthest sea, in the land of Edom.
And with the ship Hiram sent some of his servants, skilled sailors who knew how to handle ships, to be at sea with Solomon's servants.
And they went to Ophir and brought back from there four hundred and twenty talents of gold, and they brought it to King Solomon.
And the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon and of the name of the Lord, and she came to test him with riddles.

And she came to Jerusalem with a very great retinue and with camels, which were loaded with incense, a great deal of gold, and precious stones. And she came to Solomon and told him everything that was in her heart.
And Solomon explained all her words to her, and there was no matter hidden from the king that he did not explain to her.
And the queen of Sheba saw all the wisdom of Solomon, and the house that he had built,

and Solomon's food, and the seating of his servants, and the order of his attendants, and his apparel, and his cupbearers, and his eunuchs, and his offerings, which the king offered in the house of the Lord. And she was amazed.
And she said to King Solomon: "The report that I heard in my own land was true

about your words and your wisdom. I did not believe those who told me until I came myself and saw with my own eyes. And look, they did not tell me even half about your wisdom; good has been added [?] beyond all the report that I heard in my own land.
Happy are your wives, happy are your servants who stand before you and always hear your wisdom.

And blessed be the Lord your God, who was pleased with you and gave you the throne of Israel. Because the Lord loved Israel as his inheritance forever, he set you as king over them to do judgment and justice among them."

And she gave Solomon a hundred and twenty talents of gold, a very great quantity of incense, and precious stones. Never had more fragrant incense been brought there than what the queen of Sheba presented to King Solomon.
And Hiram's ship, which carried gold from Ophir, also brought unhewn timber and very precious stones.

And King Solomon made the unhewn timber into supports for the temple of the Lord and for the king's house, and into harps and lyres for the singers. No such unhewn timber had ever been brought into the land, up to this day.
And King Solomon gave the queen of Sheba everything she wanted and asked for, besides what she had presented to King Solomon.
And the weight of the gold from the gifts brought to Solomon in a single year was six hundred and sixty-six weights of gold,
apart from the tributes that had been fixed, and what came from the merchants who traded [?], and from the kings beyond the rivers, and from the governors of that land.
And King Solomon made three hundred spears of beaten gold, with three hundred drachmas on each spear.
And he made three hundred shields of beaten work, each shield covered all around with a threefold layer of gold. And the king put them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.
And King Solomon made a great throne of ivory and overlaid it with choice gold.
Its ascent had six steps. There were calves' heads on the throne at its back, arms on either side of the throne, and two lions beside the arms, one on each side.
And twelve lions stood on the steps, on either side. Nothing like it was found among all the kings.

And all the [?] vessels and utensils for service were made of gold, and the basins were of gold, and all the vessels of the House of Lebanon were overlaid with gold. There was no silver, because in the days of Solomon silver was not counted as anything.

For the king had a ship of Tarshish at sea along with Hiram's ships. Every third year the king's ship came from Tarshish and brought gold and silver, cut and uncut carbuncles, elephant tusks, apes [?], and peacocks.
And Solomon became greater than all the kings of the earth in wealth and in wisdom.
And all the kings of the earth sought to see the face of Solomon and to hear from him his wisdom, which God had put into his heart.
And each of them brought a gift: vessels of gold and of silver, clothing and myrrh, incense, and horses and mules, year by year.

And Solomon made chariots and organized horsemen, and Solomon had forty thousand mares [?] for chariots and twelve thousand horsemen. And he stationed them in the chariot cities [?] and also with the king in Jerusalem. And he was ruler over all the rulers and kings from the River as far as the land of the Philistines and as far as the border of Egypt.
And King Solomon made gold and silver in Jerusalem like stones, and pines like the wild-growing sycamores of the plain in abundance.
And Solomon's horses were brought from Egypt and from Tekoa and from Damascus; the king's merchants brought [?] them for a price.

And chariots came up from Egypt: one chariot for a hundred shekels of silver and one horse for fifty shekels of silver. So too for all those kings, for the king of the Hittites and for the kings of Assyria, by sea on the eastern side.

King Solomon was a lover of women, and he took many wives from among the foreigners: the daughter of Pharaoh, and Moabite, Ammonite and Edomite women, and women from Assyria, and Hittite and Amorite women,

and of the nations concerning whom the Lord had commanded the sons of Israel not to go in to them and not to take wives from them, 'lest your hearts turn aside to follow after their idols.' To these Solomon inclined and loved them.
And he had seven hundred wives and three hundred concubines, and his wives turned his heart aside.

And it came to pass in the time of Solomon's old age that his wives turned his heart aside to follow after foreign gods. And his heart was not perfect toward his Lord, as was the heart of David his father.
And Solomon went after Astarte, the abomination of the Sidonians, and after Moloch, the abomination of the sons of Ammon.
And Solomon did evil before the Lord and did not follow the Lord as David his father had.

At that time Solomon built the high place of Chemosh, the idol of the Moabites, on the mountain facing Jerusalem, and for Moloch, the idol of the sons of Ammon, and for Astarte, the abomination of the Sidonians.
And he did likewise for all his foreign wives, and he burned incense and sacrificed to their idols.
And the Lord was angry with Solomon, because he had turned his heart away from the Lord, the God of Israel, who had appeared to him twice
and had commanded him concerning this very matter that he should by no means follow after foreign gods, but keep and do what the Lord God had commanded him.

The Lord said to Solomon: "Because this has been done by you, and you have not kept my ordinances, and you have despised my commandments which I commanded you, I will surely tear the kingdom away from your hand and give it to your servant.
But in your days I will not do this, for the sake of David your father; from the hand of your son I will take it.
Yet I will not take away the whole kingdom, but I will give one portion to your son for the sake of David my servant and for the sake of Jerusalem, my city, which I have chosen."
And the Lord raised up an adversary against Solomon: Hadad the Edomite, who was of the line of the kings of Edom.
And it happened that when David was destroying Edom, and Joab, the commander of his army, went there, they killed every male in Edom.
And Joab and all Israel besieged Edom for six months, until they had killed every male in Edom.
And Hadad fled, and all his father's servants with him, and they went down to Egypt. Hadad was a small child at the time.

And the men set out and came to Paran, and took men from Paran with them, and went down from Paran to Egypt, to Pharaoh, the king of the Egyptians. And Hadad went to Pharaoh, and Pharaoh gave him a house, assigned him a regular allowance of provisions, and gave him land.
And Hadad found favour with Pharaoh, and Pharaoh gave him as a wife his own wife's sister, the elder sister of Tahpenes.
And the sister of Tahpenes bore Hadad a son, Genubath, and Tahpenes brought him up among Pharaoh's sons. And Genubath lived in Pharaoh's house, among Pharaoh's sons.
Hadad heard that David had slept with his fathers, and that Joab, the commander of his army, had also died. And Hadad said to Pharaoh: "Let me go, so that I may go back to my own land."
Pharaoh said to Hadad: "What do you lack here with me, that you want to go to your own land?" And Hadad said to him: "Please, just let me go!" And Hadad returned to his own land.
And the Lord raised up as adversaries against Solomon Hadad the Edomite and Rezon, the son of Eliada, who had fled from his lord Hadadezer, the king of Zobah.
And men gathered to them, leaders of a band drawn from the survivors of those whom David had slaughtered, and they went to Damascus. And Hadad was established as king in Damascus.
And he was an adversary of Israel all the days of Solomon. This is the harm to Solomon that Hadad did: he stirred up great anger in Israel, and he reigned over the land of the Edomites.

And there was Jeroboam, the son of Nebat, an Ephrathite, from Samaria. His mother's name was Sarua, and she was a widow. This widow's son was a servant of Solomon, and he raised his hand against Solomon.
And this was the reason he raised his hand against King Solomon: he built the high places and enclosed the broken-down walls of David his father.
And Jeroboam was a man of great strength. When Solomon saw that he was a capable worker, he put him in charge of the burden-bearers of the house of Joseph.

And at that time, as Jeroboam was going out of Jerusalem, the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite saw him and led him aside from the road. Ahijah was dressed in a new garment, and the two of them were alone in that place.
And Ahijah took hold of his new garment and tore it into twelve pieces.
And he said to Jeroboam: "Take these ten pieces for yourself, for this is what the Lord God of Israel says: 'I am going to tear the kingdom out of Solomon's hand and give the ten parts to you.'"
"'And the two parts shall remain his, for the sake of David my servant and for the sake of Jerusalem, my city, which I chose out of all the tribes of Israel.'"

"'This is because he has forsaken me and worshipped Astarte, the abomination of the Sidonians, and Chemosh, the idol of Moab, and Moloch, the abomination of the Ammonites. And he has not walked in my ways to do justice before me, with truth and uprightness, as David his father did.'"

"And I will not take his kingdom out of his hand at all, for the sake of David my servant, whom I chose, who kept my commandments and my truth. And I will surely set myself against Solomon all the days of his life.
"And I will take the kingdom out of his son's hand and give you ten tribes.
"And I will give the two tribes to his son, so that a lamp of my servant David may remain before me all the days in the city of Jerusalem, which I chose as a dwelling place for my name.
"And I will take you, and you shall reign over all that your soul has desired in its heart, and you shall be king over Israel.

"And it shall be, if you keep my commandments, all that I command you, and walk in my ways, and do what is upright before me, keeping all my ordinances and my commandments, as David my servant walked, I will be with you and build you a sure house, as I built for David, and I will give Israel to you.
"And I will afflict the seed of David because of this, but not for all days."
And Solomon sought to kill Jeroboam. And Jeroboam arose and fled to Egypt, to Shishak (Susakim), king of the Egyptians, and he was in Egypt until Solomon died.
And the rest of the acts of Solomon, all that he did, and all his wisdom, behold, are they not written in the book of the acts of the days of Solomon?
And the time that Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel was forty years.

And Solomon slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David his father. And it came to pass, when Jeroboam the son of Nebat heard (while he was still in Egypt, since he had fled from the presence of Solomon and was living in Egypt), when he heard that Solomon had died, he set out and came to his own city, Samaria, which is in the hill country of Ephraim. And King Solomon was gathered to his fathers, and Rehoboam his son reigned in his place.
And King Rehoboam went to Shechem, for all Israel was coming to Shechem to make him king.
And the people spoke to King Rehoboam and said to him:
"Your father made this yoke harsh upon us. Now lighten for us the harsh servitude of your father and his heavy yoke that he laid upon us, and we will serve you."
The king said to them, "Go away until the third day, and then come back to me." And they went away.
And the king consulted the elders who had stood before Solomon while he was still alive, and said to them, "How do you advise me? What answer shall I give this people?"
And they spoke to him and said, "If today you become a servant to this people and serve them, and speak good words to them, they will be your servants all the days."
But Rehoboam abandoned the counsel that the elders had given him, and took counsel with the young men who had been brought up with him, who stood before him.
And he said to them, "How do you advise me, and what answer shall I give this people, who have spoken to me and said, 'Lighten for us the yoke that your father laid on us'?"

And the young men who had been brought up with him, who stood before him, spoke to him and said, "Speak thus to this people who have spoken to you and said, 'Your father made his yoke heavy upon us; now lighten it for us.' Say this to them: 'My little finger is thicker than my father's loins.'
And whereas my father commanded you with a heavy yoke, I will add to your yoke; my father disciplined you with torments, but I will discipline you with scorpions.
And all the people of Israel came to King Rehoboam on the third day, as the king had told them, saying: "Come to me on the third day."
And the king answered the people harshly, and Rehoboam abandoned the counsel of the elders, which they had given him,

and he spoke to them according to the counsel of the young men and said: "My father made your yoke heavy, and I will add to your yoke; my father disciplined you with rods, but I will discipline you with scorpions."

And the king did not listen to the people, for this turn of events was from the Lord, so that the Lord might fulfil his word, which he had spoken by the hand of Ahijah the prophet, who was a Shilonite, to Jeroboam son of Nebat.

All the people saw that the king had not listened to them, and the people answered the king and said: "We have no portion in David from now on, nor any inheritance with the son of Jesse! Go, each man to his own dwelling, O Israel! Now shepherd your own house, David, and judge it!" And Israel went away to its inheritance.
And the sons of Judah and the sons of Israel who lived in Jerusalem and in the cities of Judah set up Rehoboam as king over themselves.
And King Rehoboam sent Adoniram, who was over the tribute, and all Israel stoned him with stones, and he died. And King Rehoboam hurried to mount his chariot and fled to Jerusalem.
And Israel has despised the name of David to this day.

And when all Israel heard that Jeroboam had returned from Egypt, they sent and brought him to the assembly and made him king over Israel. And no one followed the house of David except the tribe of Judah and Benjamin alone.

And Rehoboam went into Jerusalem and gathered all the people of Judah, one hundred and twenty thousand young men who were warriors, to fight against the house of Israel and to bring the kingdom back to Rehoboam son of Solomon.
And the word of the Lord came to Shemaiah, the man of God, saying:
"Say to Rehoboam son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all Judah and Benjamin and to the rest of the people:

Thus says the Lord: Do not go up, and do not fight against your brothers, the sons of Israel. Let each man return to his own place, for this thing came from me." And they listened to the word of the Lord and called off the campaign, according to the words of the Lord.

And King Solomon was gathered to his fathers in the city of David, and Rehoboam his son reigned in his place in Jerusalem. Rehoboam was forty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Naamah, daughter of Anan, son of Nahash, king of the sons of Ammon. And he did evil before the Lord, and Rehoboam did not walk in the way of David his father.

And there was a man from Mount Ephraim, a servant of Solomon, and his name was Jeroboam. The name of his mother, Jeroboam's mother, was Sarira, a harlot. Solomon appointed him ruler of a tribe, over the tribute of the house of Joseph. Jeroboam built Sarira on Mount Ephraim for Solomon, and he had three hundred horse chariots. He built the citadel [?] with the tribute, in the name of Ephraim. He walled in the city of David, and he was raised up toward the kingship.
And Solomon sought to kill Jeroboam. Jeroboam was afraid and fled to Shishak, king of the Egyptians, and he stayed there until Solomon died.

And Jeroboam heard in Egypt that Solomon had died. He spoke into the ears of Shishak, king of the Egyptians, and said to him: “Send me away, and let me go to my own land.” Shishak said to him: “Ask for whatever you wish, and I will give it to you.”
And Shishak gave him Ano as his wife, the sister of Thekemina, his own eldest sister-in-law, and she was the greatest among the king's daughters. And she bore Jeroboam his son Abijah.

Jeroboam said to Shishak: “Truly let me go, and let me depart.” So Shishak sent him away, and Jeroboam came out of Egypt and came to Samaria, to Mount Ephraim, and the whole tribe of Ephraim gathered there to Jeroboam. And Jeroboam built a camp there.
And he went to Shechem, which is on Mount Ephraim, and gathered there all the tribes of Israel. And Rehoboam, son of Solomon, went up.

And the word of the Lord came to Shemaiah the Selonite, and said to him: “Take a new garment that has not been put into water, and tear it into twelve pieces before you put it on, and give Jeroboam ten of the pieces to put on.” And Jeroboam took them, and Shemaiah said to him: “Thus says the Lord: You shall reign over the ten tribes of Israel.”

And the people said to Rehoboam, son of Solomon: “Your father made his yoke heavy on us and increased the food of his table. Now lighten it for us, and we will serve you.” Rehoboam said to the people: “Wait for me three more days, and I will give you an answer.”

And Rehoboam said: “Bring the elders in to me, and I will consult them about what answer I should give them after three days.” Rehoboam spoke into the ears of the people [?], telling them what the people had sent to him, and the elders of the people said to him: “Speak to the people kindly, like this.”

But Rehoboam rejected their counsel, and it did not please him. He sent and had those who had been brought up with him seized and brought before him, and he told them the same thing, saying: “This is what the people have sent to me.” And those who had been brought up with him said to him: “Speak to the people like this, and say: ‘My little finger is thicker than my father's loins. My father punished you with rods, but I will rule you with scorpions.’”
And this speech pleased Rehoboam, and he answered the people just as the young men who had been brought up with him had advised.

And all the people spoke as one man, each to his neighbour, and all the people cried out and said: “We have no share in David, and no inheritance with the son of Jesse. Each of you go to your own dwelling, Israel!”

And all the people left Shechem, and each went to his own dwelling. And Rehoboam held firm [?] and went and mounted his chariot and entered Jerusalem, and all the people of Judah and Benjamin followed him.
And it came to pass at the turn of the second year that Rehoboam gathered all the people of Judah and of Benjamin and went up to Shechem to fight against Jeroboam.

And the word of the Lord came to Shemaiah, the man of God, saying: Say to Rehoboam king of Judah, and to all the house of Judah and of Benjamin, and to the rest of the people: Do not go up, and do not fight against your brothers, the sons of Israel. Let every man return to his own home, for this thing has come from me.
And they listened to the word of the Lord and gave up going up, as the Lord had said.
And Jeroboam built Shechem, which is in the hill country of Ephraim, and lived in Shechem. And he went out from there and built Penuel.
And Jeroboam said in his heart: Now the kingdom will go back to the house of David.
If this people goes up to offer their sacrifices at the temple of the Lord in Jerusalem, the heart of the people will turn back to their lord Rehoboam, king of Judah.

And Jeroboam took counsel, and went and made two golden heifers. And Jeroboam said to the people: You have gone up to Jerusalem long enough. Behold your gods, O Israel, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt.
And he set up one of them in Bethel, and the other he gave to Dan.
This thing became a sin in [?] Jerusalem. And the people went before the one as far as Dan, and before the other to Bethel.
And Jeroboam made temples on the high places and appointed various priests who were not of the sons of Levi.

And Jeroboam held a feast in the eighth month, on the fifteenth day of the month, like the feast in Judah. And he went up to the altar that he had made in Bethel to [?] the heifers that he had made. And in Bethel he appointed priests for the high places that he had made.

And Jeroboam went up to the altar that he had built, on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, at the feast that he had made up in his own heart. And it was a feast for the sons of Israel, and he went up to the altar to sacrifice.
And behold, a man of God came from Judah to Bethel at the word of the Lord, while Jeroboam was standing at the altar to sacrifice.

And the man of God cried out against the altar at the word of the Lord and said: O altar, altar! Thus says the Lord: Behold, a son is to be born to the house of David, and his name is Josiah. And on you he will slaughter those priests of the high places and those who offer sacrifice on you, and human bones will be burned on you.
And on that day he gave a sign, saying: This is the word that the Lord has spoken: Behold, this altar will split apart, and the fat that is on it will be poured out.

And when the king heard these words of the man of God, who had cried out against the altar that was in Bethel, the king stretched out his hand from the altar and said: Seize him! And the hand that he had stretched out against him withered, and he could not draw it back again.
And the altar split apart, and its fat was poured out from the altar, as the sign that the man of God had given at the word of the Lord said it would be.

The king answered and said to the man of God: Entreat the face of the Lord your God and pray for me, so that my hand may be restored to me. And the man of God entreated the face of the Lord, and the king's hand was restored and became as it had been before.
The king spoke to the man of God and said: "Come home with me and eat bread with me, and I will give you a gift."
And the man of God said to the king: "Even if you give me half of your house, I will not go in with you, and I will not eat bread or drink water in that place.
For this is what the Lord commanded me by word, and he said to me: 'You shall not eat bread or drink water, and you shall not go back by the road by which you came.'"
So he went away by another road, and he did not go back by the road by which he had come to Bethel.

There was another prophet living in Bethel, an old man. His sons came and told him everything the man of God had done that day in Bethel, and the words he had spoken to the king. And they turned their father's face.
Their father spoke to them and said: "Which road did he take?" And his sons showed him the road by which the man of God who had come from the land of Judah had gone.
He said to his sons: "Saddle the ass for me!" So they saddled the ass for him, and he mounted it.
He went off after the man of God and found the man of God sitting under an oak. He said to him: "Are you the man of God who came from the land of Judah?" And he said: "I am!"
He said to him: "Come with me and eat bread!"
He said to him: "I am not allowed to go with you, and I will not eat bread or drink water in this place,
for this is what the Lord commanded me by word, and he said to me: 'Do not eat bread there, do not drink water, and do not come back by the road by which you go.'"

He said to him: "I too am a prophet like you, and an angel spoke to me by the word of the Lord and said to me: 'Bring him back with you to your house, and let him eat bread and drink water.'" And so he deceived him.
He brought him back, and he ate bread and drank water in his house.
And while they were sitting at the table, the word of the Lord came to the man who had brought him back.

He spoke to the man of God who had come from the land of Judah and said: "Thus says the Lord: Because you have defied the words of the Lord and have not kept the commandments that the Lord your God commanded you,

but came back and ate bread and drank water in this place, of which the Lord spoke to you and said to you: 'Do not eat bread and do not drink water,' therefore your body will not enter the tomb of your fathers."
After he had eaten bread and drunk water, he saddled his ass and turned back.
As he went, a lion met him on the road and killed him. His body lay thrown down on the road. The ass stood beside it, and the lion also stood near the body.
Some men were passing by and saw the corpse lying thrown down on the road, with the lion standing near the corpse. The men went and told it in the city where the old prophet lived.

The one who had brought him back from the road heard it and said: "This is the man of God who defied the words of the Lord. So the Lord gave him to the lion, and it mauled him and killed him, according to the word of the Lord that he spoke to him."
He spoke to his sons and said: "Saddle the ass for me." And they saddled it.
He went and found his body lying on the road, with the ass and the lion standing beside the corpse. The lion had not eaten the corpse, nor had it mauled the ass.
And the old prophet took up the body of the man of God, laid it on the donkey and brought it to the city.
And he laid his body in his own tomb, and mourned him and said: "Alas, brother!"

And after he had buried him, he spoke to his sons and said: "When I die, bury me in the tomb in which the man of God is buried, and lay me beside his bones, so that my bones may be saved along with his bones."
"For the word that he spoke by the word of the Lord against the altar that is in Bethel, and against the houses of the high places that are in Samaria, will surely come to pass."

And after this thing Jeroboam still did not turn from his wickedness. Instead he went back and made some of the people priests of the high places: whoever he wished, the king would fill his hand, and that man would become a priest of the high places.
And this thing became a sin for the house of Jeroboam, leading to its destruction and its ruin from the face of the earth.

And the Lord said to Ahijah: "Behold, the wife of Jeroboam is coming to you to ask a word from you about her son, for he is sick. Speak to her in this way." And when she came into the city of Ahijah the Shilonite, she was disguising herself.

And Ahijah said to a servant: "Go out and meet Ano, the wife of Jeroboam, and say to her: 'Come in. Why are you standing outside? For thus says the Lord: I will send a harsh thing upon you.'" And Ano came to the man of God. When Ahijah heard the sound of her footsteps as she came in, at the opening of the door, he said to her: "Come in, wife of Jeroboam. Why are you hiding yourself from me? I am a messenger of harsh news to you. And why have you brought me bread and [?] and cakes and a jar of honey?"
"Go and say to Jeroboam: Thus says the Lord God of Israel: Because I raised you up from among the people and made you ruler over my people Israel,

and I took the kingdom away from the house of David and gave it to you, yet you [?] did not act like my servant David, who kept my commandments and followed me with all his heart, doing what was upright in my eyes,
but you have done more evil than all who were before you, and you turned and made for yourself other gods, molten images, to provoke me to anger, and you forsook me and turned your back on me,

therefore, behold, I will bring evil upon the house of Jeroboam, and I will destroy every male belonging to Jeroboam (literally 'whoever urinates against the wall'), whether shut up or left free in Israel. And I will clear out what remains of the house of Jeroboam, as a garden is weeded, until it is destroyed.
Those of Jeroboam's family who die in the city the dogs shall eat, and those of his who die in the open field the birds of the sky shall eat, for the Lord has spoken.

"And you, get up and go to your house, for thus says the Lord: Behold, you will leave me, and the moment you enter the city the child will die. Your maidservants will come out to meet you and will say to you: 'The child has died.'"
"And all Israel will mourn him and bury him, for he alone of Jeroboam's family will go into a grave, because in him something good toward the Lord God of Israel was found in the house of Jeroboam."
And the Lord will raise up for himself a king over Israel, who will strike down the house of Jeroboam on that day, both from now on and even now.

The Lord will strike Israel and shake it, as a reed is shaken in the water. They will uproot Israel from the good land that he gave to their fathers and scatter them beyond the River, because they made sacred groves for themselves to provoke the Lord to anger.
And the Lord will give Israel into the hands of its enemies because of the sins of Jeroboam, who sinned and made Israel sin.
When Jeroboam's wife heard these words, she got up and left, and came to Samaria. As she was entering the gates of the house, the child died, and the sound of wailing came to meet her ears.
They buried him, and all Israel mourned for him, according to the word of the Lord which he had spoken through his servant Ahijah the prophet.
As for the words of Jeroboam, how he fought and how he reigned, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.
The days that Jeroboam reigned were twenty-two years. Then Jeroboam slept with his fathers, and his son Nabat reigned in his place.

Rehoboam son of Solomon reigned over Judah and Benjamin. Rehoboam was forty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for seventeen years in the city of Jerusalem, which the Lord God had chosen out of all the tribes of Israel to put his name there. His mother's name was Naamah.
Rehoboam did evil before the Lord. He provoked [the Lord] to jealousy by doing all that his fathers had done and by following the sins they had committed,
for they had built high places, pillars and sacred groves on every high hill and under every shady tree.
There was a conspiracy in their land, and they practised all the abominations of the nations whom the Lord God had driven out before the sons of Israel.
In the fifth year of Rehoboam's reign, Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem.

He carried off all the treasures of the house of the Lord and the treasures of the king's house. He also carried off everything else: the golden shields and the bands that David had taken from the hands of the servants of Hadadezer king of Zobah and brought to Jerusalem. Shishak carried off all of it. He also carried off all the golden armour that Solomon had made.
In their place King Rehoboam made armour of bronze. The chiefs of the runners who guarded the gates of the house of the Lord would take it up,
and they would carry it with the runners and lay [?] it in the tekua [?] of the runners.
As for the rest of the words of Rehoboam and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
There was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all their days.
Rehoboam slept with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the city of David. His son Abijah reigned in his place.
In the eighteenth year of the reign of Jeroboam son of Nebat, Abijah son of Rehoboam began to reign over Judah.
He reigned for six years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Maacah, daughter of Absalom.
He walked in the sins of his father's house, which his father had committed before him. His heart was not fully devoted to the Lord his God, as the heart of his father David had been.
For the Lord gave David a sign in Jerusalem, so that he would establish his sons after him and make Jerusalem secure,
because David did what was upright before the Lord, and all the days of his life he did not turn aside from anything the Lord had commanded him, except only in the matter of Uriah the Hittite.
And there was war between Abijah and Jeroboam all the days.
And the rest of the words of Abijah, and all that he did: behold, are they not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Judah?
And Abijah slept with his fathers in the city of David. In the twentieth year of Jeroboam, Asa his son reigned over Israel in his place.
In the twenty-first year of the king of Israel, Asa reigned over Judah.
And Asa reigned over Israel for forty-one years, and his mother's name was Anna, the daughter of Absalom.
And Asa did what was upright before the Lord, as David his father had done.
And he removed the monuments from the land and destroyed all the inventions of his fathers that had been made.

And he removed Anna his mother, so that she would no longer be ruler, because she held an assembly in the grove. And Asa cut it down, along with all the hidden places of her worship, and burned it with fire in the Valley of Cedars.
But he did not remove the high places; yet the heart of Asa was not perfect with the Lord his God all his days.
And Asa brought into the temple of the Lord the pillars of his father and his own pillars of silver and gold, and he brought silver, gold and vessels into the house of the Lord.
And there was war between Asa and Baasha, king of Israel, all the days, against Judah.
And he built Ramah, so that no one could go out or come in to Asa, king of Judah.

And Asa took the silver and gold, as much as he found in the treasuries of the king's house, and gave it into the hands of his servants. And King Asa sent it to the son of Ader, son of Tabrimmon, son of Hezion, king of Syria, who lived in Damascus, and said:

"Let there be a covenant between you and me, and between my father and your father. Behold, I have sent you a gift of gold and silver. Come and break your covenant with Baasha, king of Israel, so that he will withdraw from me."

Ader, the son of Hezion, listened to King Asa and sent the commanders of his forces against the cities of Israel. He struck Ijon, Dan, Abel-maim, all the land of Chinnereth, and as far as all the land [?] of Naphtali.
And when Baasha, king of Israel, heard this, he stopped building Ramah and returned to Tirzah.

And King Asa commanded all Judah to go to Anakim [?], and they carried away the stones of Ramah and its timbers, with which Baasha had been building. And with them Asa built the hill of Benjamin and the watchtower.

And the rest of the words of Asa, and all his mighty deeds that he did, and the cities that he built: behold, are they not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Judah? But in the time of his old age Asa did evil before the Lord, and his feet became diseased.
And Asa slept with his fathers and was buried with his fathers, and Jehoshaphat his son reigned in his place.
And Nadab son of Jeroboam became king over Israel in the third year of Asa, king of Judah. Nadab reigned over Israel for two years.
And he did evil before the Lord and walked in the ways of his father and in his sins, by which he had made Israel sin.
Baasha son of Ahijah, of the house of Bedama, which is of Issachar, surrounded him; the army was besieging Gibbethon of the Philistines, and Nadab and all the men of Israel were besieging Gibbethon.
And Baasha killed him in the fourth year of Asa, king of Judah, and Baasha reigned over Israel.

And when he became king, he destroyed the whole house of Jeroboam and did not leave a single soul belonging to Jeroboam, until he had wiped them out, according to the word of the Lord which he spoke by the hand of his servant Ahijah the Shilonite,
because of the sins of Jeroboam, by which he made Israel sin, and because of the provocation with which they provoked the Lord, the God of Israel, to anger.
And the rest of the acts of Nadab and all that he did, are they not, behold, written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
In the twenty-fifth year of Asa, king of Judah, Baasha son of Ahijah became king over Israel in Tirzah, and he reigned twenty-four years.
And Baasha did evil before the Lord and walked in the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat and in his sins, by which he had made Israel sin.
And the word of the Lord came to Jehu son of Hanani concerning Baasha, king of Israel, and said:

"Because I raised you up from the dust and gave you rule over my people Israel, and you have walked in the way of Jeroboam and have made my people Israel sin, provoking me to anger with their vain things,
behold, I will bring up evil after Baasha and after his house, and I will make his house like the house of Jeroboam.
Those of Baasha's who die in the city the dogs shall eat, and those of his who perish in the field the beasts of the earth and the birds of the sky shall eat."
And the rest of the acts of Baasha, and all that he did, and his mighty deeds, are they not, behold, written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
And Baasha slept with his fathers and was buried in Tirzah, and Elah his son reigned in his place in the twenty-ninth year of Asa, king of Judah.

The Lord spoke by the hand of Jehu son of Hanani concerning Baasha and against his house, and against all his wickedness that he did before the Lord, provoking him to anger with the works of his hands, so that it would become like the house of Jeroboam, because of the slaughter of the people of Asa, king of Judah.
And Elah son of Baasha reigned over Israel in Tirzah for two years.
And Zimri, the commander of half the chariotry, gathered the people against him while he was drinking and getting drunk in the house of Osa the steward, which was in Tirzah.
And Zimri went in and struck him and killed him, and reigned in his place.
When Zimri began to reign, as soon as he sat on his throne, he destroyed the house of Baasha,
according to the word which the Lord spoke against the house of Baasha by the hand of the prophet Jehu son of Hanani,
because of all the sins of Baasha and of Elah his son, who made Israel sin, provoking him to anger with their vain things.
And the rest of the acts of Elah and all that he did, are they not, behold, written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
In the thirty-first year of the reign of Asa, king of Judah, Zimri reigned in Tirzah for seven days, and the camp of Israel was at Gibbethon of the Philistines.
The people heard it, and they said: "Zimri has conspired and has killed King Elah." And on that day, in the camp, the people made Zimri, the chief of the people, king over Israel.
