And Zimri went up from Gibbethon, and all Israel with him, and they besieged Tirzah.
And when Zimri saw that his city was taken, he went into the inner chamber of the king's house. He set fire to the king's house, burned it over himself with fire, and died.
This was for his sins that he committed by doing evil before the Lord, for he walked in the ways of Jeroboam son of Nebat and in his sins, by which he made Israel sin.
And the rest of the acts of Zimri, and the wars that he fought, are they not, behold, written in the book of the days of the kings of Israel?
Then the people of Israel were divided. Part of them followed Tibni son of Ginath, to make him king, and part followed Zimri, to make him king.
And the people that followed Tibni son of Ginath were defeated. At that very time Tibni died, and Joram his brother. At that time Omri reigned after Tibni.
In the thirty-first year of the reign of Asa, king of Judah, Omri reigned over Israel for twelve years. He reigned in Tirzah for six years.

And Omri acquired the mountain of Samaria from Shemer, the lord of that mountain, for two talents of silver. He built on the mountain, and he named the mountain that he built Samaria, after the name of Shemer, the lord of the mountain.
And Omri did evil before the Lord, and he did worse than all who had been before him.
He walked in all the ways of Jeroboam son of Nebat and in the sins that he committed, by which he made Israel sin, provoking him to anger with their vanities.
And the rest of the acts of Omri, and all that he did, and his mighty deeds, are they not, behold, written in the book of the acts of the days of the kings of Israel?
And he slept with his fathers and was buried in Samaria. And Ahab his son reigned in his place.

And in the twelfth year of the reign of Omri, Jehoshaphat son of Asa reigned over Judah. Jehoshaphat was fifteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned in Jerusalem for twenty-five years. He entered Jerusalem at twenty-five years of age. His mother's name was Azubah, daughter of Shilhi.

And Jehoshaphat walked in the way of his father Asa. He did not turn aside from it, but did what was upright before the Lord. But Jehoshaphat did not remove the high places, for the people sacrificed and burned incense on the mountains.

And Jehoshaphat made a covenant with Ahab, king of Israel. And the rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat, and the mighty deeds that he did, and the wars that he fought, are they not, behold, written in the book of the acts of the days of the kings of Judah?
And the remaining matters and wars that there had been in the days of Asa his father, those who fought against him, he removed from the land.
And there was no king in Syria, [but] a nasib [?] [deputy?]. And King
Jehoshaphat made a ship to go to Tarshish, toward Ophir, for gold. But it did not go, because the ship was wrecked at Ezion-geber.

Then Ahab, king of Israel, said to Jehoshaphat: "Let me send my servants with your servants." But Jehoshaphat was not willing. He did evil before the Lord, and did worse than all who had been before him.
walking after the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat. He took as his wife Jezebel, daughter of Ethbaal, king of the Sidonians. And Ahab went and served Baal and worshipped him.
And he set up an altar of Baal in the house of his abominations.

And Ahab made sacred groves. Ahab multiplied provocations to provoke the Lord to anger, so that he brought his own soul to destruction, because he did more evil than all the kings of Israel who had been before him.

In his days Hiel the Bethelite built Jericho. He laid its foundation at the cost of Abiram, his firstborn, and he set up its gates at the cost of Segub, his youngest, according to the word of the Lord which he had spoken through Joshua son of Nun.

Elijah the Tishbite, who was of the seed of Gilead, said: "As the Lord God of hosts lives, the God of Israel, before whom I stand, there shall be no dew or rain in these years, except by the word of my mouth."
And the word of the Lord came to Elijah:
"Go from here toward the east and hide there by the brook Cherith, which is opposite the Jordan.
You shall drink water from the brook, and I will command the ravens to feed you there."
So Elijah went according to the word of the Lord and stayed by the brook Cherith, which is opposite the Jordan.
And the ravens brought him bread in the morning and meat in the evening, and he drank water from the brook.
After those days the brook dried up, because there was no rain on the earth.
And the word of the Lord came to Elijah, and said to him:
"Arise and go to Zarephath of Sidon and stay there. Behold, I have commanded a widow there to feed you."

So Elijah arose and went to Zarephath of Sidon and stood at the gates of the city. And behold, a widow was gathering wood. Elijah called to her and said: "Bring me a little water in a vessel, so that I may drink."
She went to fetch it, and as she went Elijah called after her and said to her: "Bring me a small morsel of bread in your hand, so that I may eat."

The woman said to him: "As the Lord your God lives, I do not have even one loaf, only one handful of flour in the jar. Behold, I am gathering wood, and I will go in and prepare it for myself and my children, and we will eat it and die."
Elijah said to her: "Do not be afraid. Go in and do as you have said, but first make me a small cake from it and bring it out to me, and afterward make some for yourself and your children.
For thus says the Lord God of Israel: The jar of flour shall not run out, and the horn of oil shall not run short, until the day the Lord gives rain on the earth."
The woman went and did just as Elijah had said. And he ate, and the woman and her children. And from that time
the jar of flour did not run out and the horn of oil did not run short, according to the word of the Lord which he had spoken through Elijah.
After this the son of the woman, the mistress of the house, fell sick. His sickness was very severe, until no breath of life remained in him.
The woman said to Elijah: "What is there between me and you, O man of God? Have you come in to bring my sins to remembrance and to put my son to death?"
And Elijah said to the woman: "Give me your son here!" And he took him from her bosom and carried him up into the upper room where he was staying, and laid him on the bed.
Elijah cried out and said: "Alas, O my Lord, witness of this widow with whom I am lodging! Have you struck her son with death?"
And he breathed on the child three times and called on the Lord and said: "O Lord, my God! Let the soul of this child return to him."
And at once he came back to life, and the child cried out.
And he brought him down from the upper room into the house and gave him to his mother, and Elijah said to her: "See, your son is alive."
And the woman said: "Behold, by this I know that you are a man of God and that the word of the Lord in your mouth is true."
And after many days, in the third year, the word of the Lord came to Elijah, and said: "Go and show yourself to Ahab, and I will give rain upon the face of the earth."
And Elijah went to show himself to Ahab. There was a severe famine in Samaria.
And Ahab summoned Obadiah, the steward, and Obadiah greatly feared the Lord.
And it happened, when Jezebel was slaughtering the prophets of the Lord, Obadiah took a hundred men of the prophets and hid them, fifty in each cave, and fed them with bread and water.

Ahab said to Obadiah: "Come, let us go out into the countryside, to the springs of water and to the valleys; perhaps we may find some grass and feed the horses and mules, so that our livestock may not perish."
And they divided the roads between them to go through them; and Ahab went by one road, and Obadiah went by another road alone.
And Obadiah was on the road alone, and behold, Elijah met him. And Obadiah hurried and got down and fell on his face, and Obadiah said: "Is it you, my lord Elijah?"
And Elijah said: "It is I. Go and tell your lord: 'Here is Elijah.'"
And Obadiah said: "How have I sinned against you, that you are handing your servant into the hands of Ahab to kill me?"

As the Lord my God lives, there is no kingdom or nation anywhere to which he has not sent to search for you, and they said: 'He is nowhere.' And he burned the kingdom and its lands, because he did not find you.
And now you tell me: 'Go and tell your lord: Here is Elijah.'

And it will happen that when I go from you, the Spirit of the Lord will carry you away to a land that I do not know. And I will go to tell Ahab, and he will not find you, and he will kill me. And your servant has feared the Lord from his youth.

Has my lord not been told what I did when Jezebel was killing the prophets of the Lord—that I took a hundred men of the prophets of the Lord and hid them, fifty and fifty in two caves, and fed them with bread and water?
And now you tell me: 'Go and tell your lord: Here is Elijah'—and he will kill me."
"As the Lord of hosts lives, before whom I stand, today I will show myself to Ahab."
And Obadiah went to meet Ahab and told him. And Ahab ran out and went to meet Elijah.
And it happened, when Ahab saw Elijah, he said to him: "Are you the [?] of Israel, who leads Israel astray?"
And Elijah said to Ahab: "It is not I who trouble Israel, but you and your father's house, for you have forsaken the Lord your God and gone after the Baals."
"Now send and gather all Israel to me at Mount Carmel, along with the prophets of falsehood, four hundred and fifty men, and the prophets of the groves, four hundred, who eat at Jezebel's table."
And Ahab sent to all Israel and gathered all the prophets of shame at Mount Carmel.

And Elijah came before all the people and said to them: "How long will you limp on both your knees? If the Lord is God, come and follow after him; if Baal is, then go after him." And the people did not answer him a word.
Elijah said to the people: "I alone am left as a prophet of the Lord, but the prophets of Baal are four hundred and fifty men, and the prophets of the groves are four hundred."

"Give us two bulls here. Let them choose one for themselves, cut it into pieces, lay it on the wood, and put no fire under it. And I will cut up the other bull, lay it on the wood, and put no fire under it."
"Then you call out in the name of your gods, and I will call on the name of the Lord my God. Whichever one answers today by fire, he is God." All the people answered and said: "What you say is good."
And Elijah said to the prophets of falsehood: "Choose one bull for yourselves, since you are many, and prepare it first. Call on the names of your gods, but put no fire under it."

And they took the one bull that he had given them and did so. They called on the name of Baal from dawn until midday, saying: "Hear us, Baal, hear us!" But there was no voice and no one listening. And they ran around the altar that they had made.

And when it was noon, Elijah mocked them and said: "Call out loudly, all of you together! Perhaps he is talking something over in his heart, or he is giving some order, or, if he is asleep, he will wake up and get up."
And they cried out with a loud voice and cut themselves with swords and lances, as was their custom, until the blood poured out over them.

And they prophesied until noon had passed. It was now just the time for offering the sacrifice, and there was no voice and no one listening. Elijah spoke to the prophets of the abominations and said: "Stand aside now, and I too will make my sacrifice." And they stood aside and went away.
Elijah said to the people: "Come to me!" And all the people came near to him.
And Elijah took twelve stones, matching the number of the twelve tribes of Israel, as the Lord had told him, and said: "Israel shall be your name!"
And he built up the stones and repaired the altar of the Lord that had been torn down. And he made a trench around the altar, big enough to hold two measures of seed, all around the altar.
And he laid the wood on the altar that he had made, and [?] on it, and cut the sacrifice into pieces and laid it on the altar.

And Elijah said to them: Bring me two jars full of water and pour it on the altar, and on the sacrifice and the wood. And he said a second time: Pour! And they poured a second time. And he said a third time: Pour! And they poured a third time.
The water ran down around the altar, and the trench was filled with water.

And just as the sacrifice was being offered up, Elijah cried out to heaven and said: O Lord, God of Abraham, and of Isaac, and of Israel! Hear me, O Lord, hear me today by fire, and let all this people know that you alone are the Lord God of Israel, and that I am your servant, and that for your sake I have done all these things.
And you have turned the heart of this people to follow you.

And fire fell from the Lord out of heaven and consumed the sacrifice, and the wood, and the water, and whatever was on it. And the fire licked up the water of the trench, and the stones, and the earth.
And all the people fell on their faces and said: Truly this is the Lord God!
And Elijah said to the people: Seize the prophets of Baal, and let none of them escape! And they seized them, and Elijah brought them down to the brook Kishon and slaughtered them there.
Elijah said to Ahab: Get up, eat and drink, for the sound of the feet of the rain is heard.
And Ahab got up to eat and drink, and Elijah went up Mount Carmel. He bowed down to the ground and put his face between his two knees.

And he said to his servant: Get up and look toward the way of the sea. And the servant looked and said: There is nothing! Elijah said to him: Go back and look seven times! And the servant looked seven times.

And at the seventh time, behold, there was a small cloud, like a man's [?], which was drawing up water from the sea. He said to the servant: Go up and say to Ahab: Harness your chariots and go down, lest the rain overtake you.
And in the meantime the sky grew dark with clouds and wind, and there was a great rain. And Ahab was weeping as he went into Jezreel.
And the hand of the Lord was upon Elijah. And he girded his loins and ran before Ahab until he entered Jezreel.
And Ahab told Jezebel all that Elijah had done, and how he had slain the prophets of Baal with the sword.

And Jezebel sent messengers to Elijah and said: If you are Elijah and I am Jezebel, may the gods do so and so to me, and add this to me, for at this same hour tomorrow I will make your head like the head of one of them.
And Elijah was afraid, and he got up and fled for his life, and he came to Beersheba, which belongs to Judah, and left his servant there.
And he went on a day's journey into the wilderness, and he sat down under a [?] tree and said: Let it be enough now, O Lord; take my soul from me, for I am no better than my fathers.
And he lay down there and slept under the plant. And behold, someone touched him with a hand and said to him: Get up and eat.
He looked and saw by his head a cake of [?] and water in a jar. And Elijah got up, ate and drank, and turned over and slept again.
The angel came back a second time, touched him, and said to him: Get up, eat and drink, for the journey is far too long for you.
And he got up, ate and drank, and in the strength of that food he went forty days and forty nights as far as Mount Horeb.
And he went into a cave there and stayed there. And behold, the voice of the Lord came to him and said to him: "What are you doing here, Elijah?"

And Elijah said: "I have been very zealous for the Lord God Almighty, for the sons of Israel have forsaken you. They have torn down your altars and killed your prophets with the sword. I alone am left, and they are seeking my life, to take it."

The Lord said to him: "Go out tomorrow and stand before the Lord on that mountain. And behold, the Lord will pass by." And there was a great and strong wind, which tore the mountains apart and shattered the rocks before the Lord, but the Lord was not in the wind. After the wind there was an earthquake, but the Lord was not in the earthquake.
And after the earthquake there was a fire, but the Lord was not in the fire. And after the fire there was the sound of a gentle breeze, and the Lord was in it.
And when Elijah heard it, he covered his face with his mantle, went out and stood by the cave. And a voice came to him and said: "What are you doing here, Elijah?"

And Elijah said: "I have been very zealous for the Lord God Almighty, for the sons of Israel have forsaken you. They have torn down your altars and killed your prophets with the sword. I alone am left, and they are seeking my life, to take it."
The Lord said to him: "Go, return on your way, and go by the desert road to Damascus, and anoint Hazael as king over Syria.
And anoint Jehu son of Nimshi [?] as king over Israel, and anoint Elisha son of Shaphat as prophet in your place.
And whoever escapes the sword of Hazael, Jehu will kill, and whoever escapes the sword of Jehu, Hazael will kill.
And I will leave in Israel seven thousand men whose knees have not bowed to Baal, and every mouth that has not worshipped him."

And Elijah went away from there and found Elisha son of Shaphat. He was ploughing with twelve yoke of oxen in front of him, and he was with the twelfth of them. And Elijah came up to Elisha and threw his mantle over Elisha.
And Elisha ran after Elijah and said to him: "Let me kiss my father and my mother, and then I will follow you." And Elijah said: "Go back, for so be it for you."

And Elisha went back from him, took the yoke of oxen, slaughtered them, and boiled them with the oxen's gear, and gave the meat to the people, and they ate. And Elisha rose up, went, followed Elijah, and served him.

And the son of Hadad, king of Syria, gathered all his people and came and surrounded Samaria, and thirty-two kings were with him, with horses and chariots. And they came up, surrounded it and fought against it.
And the son of Hadad, king of Syria, sent messengers to Ahab, king of Israel,
and said to him: "Thus says the son of Hadad: 'Your silver and your gold are mine, and your wives and your best children are mine.'"
The king of Israel answered and said: "As you say, my lord the king, I and all that I have are yours."
And then the messengers came back again and said: "Thus says the son of Hadad: 'I sent to you and said to you: Give me your silver and your gold and your wives,

for tomorrow, at this very hour, I will send my servants to you, and they will search your houses and the houses of your servants. And everything that their eyes desire, on which they lay their hand, they will take away.'"
Ahab called all the elders of Israel and said to them, "Know now and see that this man is seeking evil. He sent to me for my wives and for my children, and I did not hold back my silver and my gold."
And the elders and all the people said to him, "Do not listen, and do not consent."

And the king of Israel said to the messengers of Ben-hadad, "Say this to your lord the king: 'Everything you sent to your servant for the first time I have done, but this word I cannot do.'" And the messengers went away and reported this word.
And Ben-hadad sent again and said, "May God do this to me and add more to it, if the dust of Samaria is enough for the handfuls [?] of all the people, my foot soldiers."
The king of Israel answered and said, "Enough for you! Let the hunchback not boast like one whose back is straight."
And when he gave this answer, Ben-hadad was drinking, and all who were with him, in the tents. He said to his servants, "Set up the army," and they laid siege around the city.

And behold, a prophet came to the king of Israel and said, "Thus says the Lord: Have you seen all this great multitude? Behold, I will give it into your hands today, and you will know that I am the Lord."
And Ahab said to him, "By whom?" And he said, "Thus says the Lord: by the young men of the rulers of the districts." And Ahab said, "Who will do the fighting?" And he said to him, "You."

And Ahab counted the young men of the rulers who were drawn up, and they were two hundred and thirty-two, and King Iezer [?] was with him. After this he reviewed all the people, the men of might, seventy thousand.
And the king went out with them at midday, while Ben-hadad was drinking and getting drunk in Succoth, he and the thirty-two kings with him, his allies.
And the rulers and the young men of the rulers of the districts went out first. And they sent word to the king of Assyria and told him, "Men have come out of Samaria."
And the king of Assyria said to them, "If they come out for peace, take them alive."
And the young men of the rulers of the districts came out and gathered from the city, and the army behind them.
And each man struck the one he met, and struck a second time the one opposite him [?]. And the Assyrians fled, and Israel pursued them, and Ben-hadad, king of Assyria, escaped on horseback.
And the king of Israel went out and took the horses and chariots, and struck Assyria with a great slaughter.
And a prophet came to the king of Israel and said to him, "Strengthen yourself, and know and see what you are to do, for at the turn of the year Ben-hadad, king of Assyria, will come up against you."

And the servants of the king of Assyria said to their lord, "The God of Israel is a god of the mountains and not a god of the valleys, and that is why they were stronger than we. If we fight them on level ground, we will be stronger than they.
Do this according to our word: send these kings away, each to his own place, and appoint commanders in their place.

And replace the army that fell from you, horses like those horses and chariots like those chariots, and we will fight them on level ground and be stronger than they." And he listened to their voice and did so.
And at the turn of the year Ben-hadad reviewed the people of Assyria, and he gathered them and went up to Aphek to fight Israel.
And the sons of Israel were counted and made ready, and they set out and went to meet them. And Israel encamped before them like two flocks of goats, while Syria filled the land.

And a man of God came and said to the king of Israel: "Thus says the Lord: Because Syria has said, 'The God of Israel is a God of the mountains, and he is not a God of the valleys,' I will now give that great people into your hands, and you shall know that I am the Lord, the God of Israel."
And the sons of Israel encamped opposite them for seven days. And after the seven days they drew up for battle, and Israel slew a hundred and twenty thousand Syrian foot soldiers in one day.

And the rest fled to the city of Aphek, and the wall fell on twenty-seven thousand of the men who were left and killed them. And Ben-hadad fled and went into a house, into an inner chamber, a storeroom.

And he said to his servants: "I know that the kings of Israel are merciful kings. Let us gird ourselves with sackcloth and put ropes on our heads, and go out to the king of Israel; perhaps he will spare our lives."

And they girded sackcloth on their loins and bound ropes on their heads, and they went out and said to the king of Israel: "Your servant Ben-hadad says: Spare my life." And Ahab said to them: "Is he still alive? He is my brother."

And the men took this as an omen. They acted quickly, caught the word from his mouth, and said: "Your brother Ben-hadad." And Ahab said to them: "Bring him out." And Ben-hadad came out, and they took him up into the chariot with him.

And the king of Syria said to Ahab: "The cities that my father took from your father I will give to you, and you shall impose tribute for yourself on Damascus, just as my father imposed it on Samaria, and I will let you go under a covenant." And he made a covenant with him and sent him away with his household, and he went away from him.
And a certain man from among the sons of the prophets said to his companion by the word of the Lord: "Strike me!" But the man refused to strike him.
The prophet said to him: "Because you did not obey the word of the Lord, behold, you will go away from me and a lion will kill you." And he went away from him, and a lion found him and killed him.
And the prophet met another man and said to him: "Strike me!" And the man struck him, and when he struck him he wounded him badly.
And the prophet went and stood waiting for the king of Israel by the road, and he tied a bandage over his eyes.

And as the king was just passing by, he cried out to the king and said: "Your servant had gone out into the [?] to fight, and a man brought a man to me and said to me, 'Guard this man for me. If he escapes from you and goes away, your life shall be forfeit in place of his life, or else you shall give me a talent of silver.'
"And while your servant was looking this way and that, he was nowhere to be found." And the king of Israel said to him: "Look, you yourself now stand judged before me: you have indeed killed him."
And he quickly pulled the bandage off his eyes, and the king recognized him as one of the prophets.

And he said to Ahab: "Thus says the Lord: Because you let a man doomed to death go free from your hand, behold, your life shall be forfeit in place of his life, and your people in place of his people."
And the king of Israel came to his house grieved and dejected, weeping, and he entered Samaria.
And after these things, there was a vineyard that belonged to Naboth the Jezreelite, beside the house of Ahab, king of Samaria.

And Ahab spoke to Naboth and said to him: "Give me your vineyard, so that it may be my vegetable garden, because it is close to my house, and I will give you another vineyard. If it is pleasing to you, I will give you silver in exchange for your vineyard, and it will be my vegetable garden."
Naboth said to Ahab: "The Lord my God forbid that I should give away the inheritance of my fathers."

And Ahab came to his house grieved and dejected because of the word that Naboth the Jezreelite had spoken, for he had said: "I will not give you the inheritance of my fathers." And Ahab's spirit was grieved because of this word; he lay down on his bed, covered his face, and did not eat bread.
And Jezebel his wife went in to him and said to him: "Why is your spirit grieved, and why do you not eat bread?"

Ahab said to her: "Because I spoke to Naboth the Jezreelite and said to him: 'Give me your vineyard for a price in silver; if you do not want that, I will give you another vineyard in its place.' And he said to me: 'I will not give you the inheritance of my fathers.'"
Jezebel his wife said to him: "Is this how you now exercise kingship over Israel? Arise, eat bread, and be yourself again, and I will give you the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite."
And she wrote a letter in Ahab's name, sealed it with his seal, and sent the letter to the elders and the nobles who lived with Naboth.
This was written in the letter, and it said: "Proclaim a fast, and seat Naboth at the head of the people.
And seat two sons of lawless men before him, and let them testify against him and say: 'Naboth blessed God and the king!' And bring him out of the city, and let him die."
And the men of that city, the elders and the nobles who lived in his city, did so, just as Jezebel had sent the messenger to them.
And they proclaimed a fast and seated Naboth at the head of the people.

The two men, sons of lawlessness, came forward and sat before him, and they testified against him, saying: "You blessed God and the king." And they led him out of the city and stoned him, and he died.
And they sent word to Jezebel and said to her: "Naboth has been stoned and has died."
And Jezebel said to Ahab: "Arise now and take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, who would not give it to you for silver; for Naboth is not alive, but has died."
And when Ahab heard that Naboth had died, he tore his garments and put on sackcloth. And after that Ahab arose and went down to the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite to take possession of it.
And the Lord said to Elijah the Tishbite:
"Arise and go down to meet Ahab, king of Israel, who is in Samaria; for behold, he has seized the vineyard of Naboth and has gone down to take possession of it.

And say to him: 'Thus says the Lord: Because you have killed Naboth and taken possession of his vineyard, therefore thus says the Lord: In the place where the pigs and the dogs licked the blood of Naboth, there the pigs and the dogs shall lick your blood, and harlots shall bathe in your blood.'"

And Elijah came to Ahab, and Ahab said to Elijah: "Have you found me, my enemy?" And Elijah said: "I have found you, because you have sold yourself for nothing to do evil before the Lord and to provoke him to anger."

"Therefore the Lord says this: 'Behold, I will bring evil upon you, and I will kindle a fire after you, and I will destroy every male of Ahab's, everyone who pisses against the wall, the one shut up and the one left in Israel.'"

"'And I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat, and like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah, for all the provocations with which you have provoked me to anger and made Israel sin.'"
"And concerning Jezebel the Lord says: 'The dogs shall eat her by the wall of Jezreel.'"
"'Whoever of Ahab's dies in the city, the dogs shall eat; and whoever of his dies in the field, the birds of the sky shall eat.'"
For there was no one like Ahab, who sold himself to do evil before the Lord, as Jezebel his wife had turned him.
And he became exceedingly abominable in going and following in the track of abominations, just like all that the Amorites did, whom the Lord destroyed before the sons of Israel.

But because of the word, Ahab was stricken with remorse before the face of the Lord; and he went about weeping, and he tore his garment and put sackcloth on his flesh and fasted. And he had put on sackcloth on the day when Jezebel killed Naboth the Jezreelite and his son. And he went about downcast.
And the word of the Lord came to Elijah concerning Ahab, and the Lord said:
"Have you seen how Ahab has repented before my face? I will not bring the evil in his days, but in the days of his son I will bring the evil."
And he remained there three years. And there was no war between the Syrians and Israel.
And it came to pass in the third year that Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, came to Ahab, king of Israel.
And the king of Israel said to his servants: "Do you not know that Ramoth Gilead is ours, and yet we keep silent and do not take it out of the hands of the king of Syria?"

The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, king of Judah: "Will you come with me to Ramoth Gilead to battle?" Jehoshaphat said to him: "As you are, so am I; as your people, so my people; and as your horses, so my horses."
Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, said to Ahab, king of Israel: "Let us also inquire of the Lord."

And the king of Israel gathered all the prophets, about four hundred men, and said to them: "Shall I go up to Ramoth Gilead to battle, or shall I refrain?" And they said: "Go up, for the Lord will surely give it into the hands of the king."
Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel: "Is there no prophet of the Lord here, so that we may inquire of the Lord through him?"

The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat: "There is one man here through whom to inquire of the Lord, but I hate him, because he does not speak good concerning me, but evil: Micaiah son of Imlah." Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, said to him: "Do not speak so, O king!"
And the king of Israel called a eunuch and said to him: "Quickly bring Micaiah son of Imlah."
And Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, and Ahab, king of Israel, were sitting each on his throne, armed, at the entrance of the gate of Samaria, and all the prophets were prophesying before them.
Zedekiah son of Chenaanah made himself a horn of iron and said: "The Lord says this: 'With this you shall gore Syria until you have finished them off.'"
And all the prophets were prophesying and saying this: "Go up to Ramoth-gilead, and the Lord will prosper you and give the king of Syria into your hands."

And the messenger who went to call Micaiah said this to him: "Look, all the prophets are prophesying and speaking good for the king with one mouth. Let your word also be like the word of one of them, and you too speak good for the king."
And Micaiah said: "As the Lord lives, whatever the Lord says to me, that is what I will speak."

And Micaiah came to the king, and the king said to him: "Shall I go up to Ramoth-gilead to battle, or shall I refrain?" Micaiah said to him: "Go up, and the Lord will give success into the king's hands."
The king said to him: "How many more times must I put you under oath to speak the truth to me in the name of the Lord?"

Micaiah said to him: "Not so. I saw all Israel scattered on the mountains like sheep that have no shepherd. And the Lord said: 'If these are steadfast toward God, let each man return to his own place in peace.'"
The king said to Jehoshaphat, king of Judah: "Did I not tell you that this man does not prophesy good concerning me, but evil?"

And Micaiah said: "Not so; rather, hear the word of the Lord. Not so. I saw the Lord God of Israel sitting on his throne, and all the hosts of heaven were standing around him, on his right and on his left."

And the Lord said: "Who will deceive Ahab, king of Israel, so that he goes up to Ramoth-gilead and falls there?" And one said this and another said that. And the Lord said: "You will not be able." And he said: "To you [?]."
And a spirit came and stood before the Lord and said: "I will deceive him." And the Lord said to him: "By what means?"
And he said: "I will go out and become a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets, and I will deceive him." The Lord said to him: "You will be able. Go out and do so."
"And now the Lord has put a lying spirit in the mouth of all these prophets of yours, and the Lord has spoken evil concerning you."
And Zedekiah, son of Chenaanah, came up and struck Micaiah on the cheek and said: "Which spirit of the Lord departed from me and spoke to you?"
And Micaiah said: "Look, you will see on that day, when you go from inner chamber to inner chamber to hide."
The king of Israel said: "Seize Micaiah and hand him over to Semier, the governor of the city, and to Joash, the king's son."
"And say: Put this man in prison, and let him eat the bread of affliction and drink the water of affliction until I return in peace."
Micaiah said to him: "If you return in peace, the Lord has not spoken to me."
And the king of Israel, and Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, with him, went up to Ramoth-gilead.
And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, king of Judah: "Clothe me, and I will go into battle; and you put on my garments." And the king of Israel disguised himself and went into battle.
And the king of Syria commanded his thirty-two chariot commanders and said to them: "Do not engage in battle with small or great, but only with the king of Israel alone."
And when his chariot commanders saw Jehoshaphat, they said: "[?], for this must be the king of Israel," and they surrounded him to fight; and Jehoshaphat cried out, and the Lord saved him.
And when the chariot commanders saw that this was not the king of Israel, they turned back from him.

And one of the archers drew his bow and struck Ahab, king of Israel, between the lung-side and the breast. And the king said to his charioteer: "Turn the chariot around with your hand and take me out of the battle, for I am wounded."

And the battle grew fierce on that day, and King Ahab stood in the chariot facing the Syrians from dawn until evening. And the blood ran down from his wound into the bottom of the chariot, and the king died in the evening.
And just as the sun was setting, the herald of the army [?] stood up and said: "Let each man go to his own city and to his own land,
for the king is dead." And they came to Samaria and buried King Ahab in Samaria.

And they washed the blood off the chariot at the river of Samaria, and the dogs licked up the blood, and the harlots washed in his blood, according to the word of the Lord which he had spoken by the hand of the prophet Elijah.

And the rest of the acts of Ahab, and all that he did, and the ivory house that he built, and all the cities that he built: are they not, behold, written in the book of the acts of the days of the kings of Israel?
And Ahab slept with his fathers, and Ahaziah his son reigned in his place.
Ahaziah son of Ahab reigned over Israel in Samaria for two years, in the twenty-fourth year of the reign of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah.
And Ahaziah did evil before the Lord, and he walked in the ways of Ahab his father, and of Jezebel his mother, and in the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who made Israel sin.
And he worshipped Baal and served him, and he provoked the Lord to anger more than all who had been before him.

After this Jehoshaphat allied himself with Ahaziah, king of Israel, and he too acted lawlessly in going to him and keeping company with him. And he joined with him in building ships, and he was sending them to Tarshish, and he built the ships at Ezion-geber.

And Eliezer son of Dodavah, who was from Mareshah, prophesied against Jehoshaphat and said: "Because you joined yourself to Ahaziah and allied yourself with him, the Lord has cut off your work." And his ships were broken up, and they could not go to Tarshish.
And Jehoshaphat slept with his fathers and was buried in the city of David, and Jehoram his son reigned in his place.
